components.name: Connected Phase Roadmap
components.description: Thin priority sequence with visible goals and native technical scope.
components.html:
1. First

    Reliable playback

    • Note and MPE handling
    • Bounded audio callbacks
    • Streaming under storage pressure
    Technical scope

    Make failures explicit and fix musical correctness before broadening compatibility claims.

    • Preserve note, family, expression and release ownership across sustain/sostenuto, MPE channel reuse, voice stealing, script-generated notes and plan replacement.
    • Complete missing MIDI 2.0 expression/management and source-specific event ordering against canonical timestamped events.
    • Finish modulation composition, envelope/LFO routing and source parameter laws; keep unsupported targets visible in load reports.
    • Establish production streaming admission, cold-onset preload, resource budgets and starvation behavior under real storage pressure.
    • Keep script execution, worker handoffs and retirement bounded; move allocation, filesystem work and destruction off audio callbacks.

    Exit evidence: regression cases exercise the actual musical behavior; callback/heap guards and real storage workloads demonstrate bounded operation; errors retain their cause and build identity. A silent fallback is not a passing result.

    Sources: ownership and scheduling, MIDI, modulation, streaming, current priorities.

  2. Next

    Kontakt

    • KSP scripts and callbacks
    • Instrument interfaces and resources
    • Effects, modulation and state recall
    Technical scope

    Translate instruments into shared services while preserving native semantics and recognizable authored interfaces.

    • Expand versioned containers, resources, samples, snapshots and instrument semantic admission with strict malformed-input boundaries.
    • Complete KSP language, callbacks, builtins and underlying services, including asynchronous operations and persistent state.
    • Resolve stored-event note-off across script stages without losing the physical key lifetime or upstream release callbacks.
    • Expand source engines, loops, filters, effects and modulation laws against reference behavior.
    • Complete generic, stock and bitmap KSP views, native control resources and requested UI generations; retain Original and Vector presentation as distinct modes.
    • Preserve multi-part routing, automation identities and state recall through the production host integration.

    Exit evidence: versioned instruments and scripts produce the expected audio, callbacks, UI interactions and recall in controlled reference comparisons. Decoding a file, displaying artwork or recognizing a builtin alone does not close the gate.

    Sources: Kontakt source boundary, KSP completion map, UI frontends, compatibility checklist.

narrative.overview:
This website extends the native graphite and Noto Sans system recorded in the root [DESIGN.md](../DESIGN.md). The native editor remains the authority for the application; this document records the web reading and download surface. Graphite fills and square edges carry through, while the website uses muted pink for interaction and donations, recognizable Discord blue for community access, and a light primary download for the detected desktop platform.

The overview keeps the message short and puts the release identity and three icon-led downloads before an uncropped image of the actual player. Shared header and footer actions make donations and community access prominent. Reading pages retain essential instructions and evidence; the roadmap uses a quiet connected phase sequence with complete implementation detail in native disclosures.
keyCharacteristics: Dark graphite surfaces with thin dividers and quiet neutral text.
Purposeful pink donation actions, Discord blue, and light detected downloads on graphite.
A bundled Noto Sans face and square page controls.
The real player screenshot as product proof, concise reading, and expandable engineering scope.

rules.name: The Native System Extension Rule
rules.body: Preserve the native editor's graphite, Noto Sans, square-edge identity; apply website-specific type scale and responsive reading layout only to this web surface.

rules.name: The Pink Signal Rule
rules.body: Use pink for donation actions, interaction, focus, first-phase priority, and partial support; keep the page foundation graphite.

rules.name: The Graphite Continuity Rule
rules.body: Keep the shared graphite palette as the page foundation and let the actual application image supply its own color.

rules.name: The One Face Rule
rules.body: Keep the bundled Noto Sans for the site's normal text and avoid adding a second display face.

rules.name: The Download First Rule
rules.body: Keep the release identity and all three platform choices ahead of the large player image.

rules.name: The Visible Scope Rule
rules.body: Preserve the support table's feature, status, and full scope text in its mobile layout.

rules.name: The Flat Plane Rule
rules.body: Use tonal fills, spacing, and hairlines for hierarchy; keep cards on the same plane as the page.

rules.name: The Square Edge Rule
rules.body: Keep controls and containers rectangular; use circular markers only for the roadmap sequence and an accent outline for keyboard focus.

rules.name: The Real Player Rule
rules.body: Let the actual application screenshot carry the product's visual detail; keep the surrounding web chrome quiet.

rules.name: The Evidence Stays Open Rule
rules.body: Within expanded support groups, keep status and its full scope visible together in each row, including at mobile widths.

dos: Do keep the website an extension of the native graphite and Noto Sans system.
Do lead the overview with the current release and all three platform downloads.
Do use the real, uncropped player screenshot as product proof.
Do preserve full evidence and phase implementation scope in keyboard-native disclosures.
Do use pinned real service and OS SVGs with text labels and working static links.
Do retain the visible scope and gaps beside support statuses on every screen size.
donts: Don't create a separate palette, rounded-card system, or shadow-heavy layer.
Don't replace the player screenshot with stock artwork or a fabricated interface.
Don't spread action colors into decorative page backgrounds or use pink as a compatibility success color.
Don't hide support gaps behind hover, tooltips, or mobile-only horizontal scrolling.
Don't turn the priority sequence into a completion chart or a promised release schedule.
